rationale: Attempt-00 (128,64,64,stages=1,swizzle=0) gave 2558.09 us / 531.63 MB DRAM; attempt-01 (64,128,64,stages=1,swizzle=16) cut simulated latency to 1616.24 us and DRAM to 269.75 MB, confirming that the serpentine swizzle hypothesis correlates with reduced simulated traffic in this simulator. Actual smem remained 32768 B in both compiled runs, so the 32768-byte portability cap stays as the shared-memory limit and all tile/stage/swizzle domains are kept feasible (all divide M=N=K=4096). Both prior tuples are excluded, so HiGHS must pick a new point. We slightly raise traffic (1.5) and pipeline (1.5) weights relative to launches/footprint because the observed latency reduction tracked DRAM reduction and stages=1 was used in both runs; testing stages>=2 with swizzle>0 is the next hypothesis, and larger tiles (block_M=128) may further reduce traffic under reuse. This remains a dimensionless proxy ranking, not a microsecond prediction. Next hypothesis: a stages=2-3, swizzle in {4,8,16}, block_M in {64,128} point should lower simulated latency further; if simulator DRAM/latency do not improve, revert weights toward uniform. Validation scope: Metal checks execute the exact source/config/TIR, CUDA binaries are not executed, and GB10 values are simulator estimates, not hardware measurements; no global optimality is claimed.
